name: quote-build
short: Builds a make-to-order quote from the intake form, past jobs and cost history, and shows where every number came from.
what: quote-build is part of the Claude for Manufacturing plugin. It loads the intake form, finds comparable past jobs, works out machine hours per operation, builds up material, labor, setup and outside processing costs, and puts margin on its own line. It checks the promised date against shop load and produces a customer quote plus an internal cost-basis sheet. When a customer counters, it revises the quote in place with a change record.
who: Estimators and owners at job shops and make-to-order plants. If you don't quote manufactured parts, skip it.
needs: Claude Code or the Claude plugin directory
An intake form and cost figures (it can run on pasted figures with no connector)
Optional: NetSuite or Infor M3, Microsoft 365 and Autodesk Fusion connected
Your labor, burden and margin rates set once through onboarding or `MFG_*` variables

steps.title: Install the plugin
steps.text: The repo README gives this command. The plugin's name is `claude-for-manufacturing`. You can also find it in the Claude plugin directory or under `/plugin > Discover`.

steps.title: Set up your plant
steps.text: Say "set us up". The onboarding skill asks which ERP, CAD, maintenance and document systems you use and learns your exports and rates.

steps.title: Ask for a quote
steps.text: The skill picks up phrases such as "build the quote", "price this job" or "quote this RFQ".

watch: The plugin is a reference implementation. It is not actively maintained and is provided as is.
Nothing reaches a customer until the estimator releases it. The quote is a document a person files and sends, and nothing is written back to the ERP.
A rate typed into a run is not used. Rates come from `MFG_*` variables or the plant profile, and lines are blocked if none is set.
With a text spec and no drawing, it produces a rough estimate, not a firm quote.
The repo README says to make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating or using it.
